info.description:
Rizqim backend API (`/api/v1`): Telegram Mini App, ega/menejer/kuryer ekranlari va to'lov webhooklari.

**Kirish:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (Laravel Sanctum). Token `POST /v1/auth/telegram` orqali olinadi.

**Javob formati:** `{ "success": bool, "message": string, "data": ... }`. Xatolarda `success: false` va `message`;
validatsiya xatolari (422) `errors` maydonida keladi.

Spetsifikatsiya koddan yaratiladi: `cd backend && php artisan api-spec:export` (`packages/api-spec/openapi.json`).

post.description:
The first code from the authenticator app turns 2FA on and opens the session. `recovery_codes` (10) are shown
only here, once: each one signs in once when the phone is lost; only their hashes are kept.

409.description: Set-up not started or 2FA already on

post.description: Replaces every recovery code with 10 new ones, shown only in this answer. Needs a step-up confirmation.

Only for a `setup_required` challenge. Returns the new secret (for manual entry), the `otpauth://` URI and the
QR code as inline SVG. The same challenge gives the same secret again; it is saved only when `2fa/confirm`
accepts a code from it, and never shown again afterwards. 409 `two_factor_already_enabled` once 2FA is on.

Send `code` (6 digits from the app) or `recovery_code` (one of the saved recovery codes: it is burnt). A code
already used, or one older than the last used, is refused (replay). Opens the session: `token` (Bearer, the
admin API only), absolute `expires_at` (12 hours); 60 minutes without a request also end it.

409.description: The account must set 2FA up first (setup_required)

post.description:
A current TOTP code marks this session confirmed for 10 minutes. Actions behind it (team and role changes,
2FA resets, new recovery codes, revoking another session; later money and order interventions) answer 403
`reauth_required` without it: ask for the code, call this, retry once.
post.summary: Step-up: confirm with a fresh code

post.description:
The invite link's token and the new password (at least 12 characters, not the email). Answers with a
`setup_required` challenge: the member goes straight on to the 2FA set-up. 422 `invite_invalid` for an
unknown, used, re-issued or expired (72 hours) link.

Returns a challenge for the second step (5 minutes, single use): `otp_required` (send the app's code to
`2fa/verify`) or `setup_required` (2FA not set up yet: `2fa/setup`, then `2fa/confirm`). An unknown email and a
wrong password get the same 422 `invalid_credentials`; a disabled member 403 `member_disabled`; too many bad
tries 429 `locked`.

403.description: Disabled member (member_disabled), or no 2FA and the set-up window (24 h after an invite or a 2FA reset) closed (setup_not_allowed)

get.description:
Who is signed in, their platform role and effective admin permissions (the admin app shows only the sections

Live sessions only (not past their 12 hours, used in the last 60 minutes), newest first; `current` is this one.

delete.description: Ending this session is a log-out; ending another one needs a step-up confirmation (403 `reauth_required`).

404.description: No such live session of mine

get.description:
The v2 plans (Start, Asosiy, Pro) in catalog order; `all=1` adds the P1-23 plans (version 1: readable, for the
stores still on them). Money as decimal strings; `features`: App\Enums\PlanFeature values the plan has (base ones
included); `subscriptions`: current subscriptions on the plan. `feature_catalog`: every feature with its label
and whether it is a base one (never gated).

put.description:
Any of `name`, `description`, `is_active` (an inactive plan cannot be assigned; its stores keep it), `monthly_fee`,
`yearly_fee`, `included_pos`, `included_kds`, `extra_pos_fee`, `extra_kds_fee` (so'm, decimal strings or numbers,
up to 2 decimals), `trial_days` (0–90, for new subscriptions), `features` (the gated features it has: a list of
App\Enums\PlanFeature values; base ones are always on), `sort_order` (its place: higher is an upgrade); `reason`
required. P1-23 plans are not changed here (404). Answers the plan.

get.description:
`store`; `subscription` (the current one or null); `entitlements` (as GET /owner/billing/entitlements);
`debt` (debt_balance, subscription_debt — unpaid invoices, commission_debt — what the credit limit counts,
credit_limit, over_credit_limit); `commission` (`rates` per channel with `source` override | plan | flat |
default, `overrides`, `flat_rate`, `delivery_courier`); `history` (subscriptions, newest first); `invoices` (the
last 24 with their lines, paid and outstanding parts and `dunning` steps).

put.description:
`overrides`: the store's own rate per channel ({"pickup": "3.00", "own_delivery": null, ...}; channels
rizqim_courier, own_delivery, pickup, pos, aggregator; a percent 0–100 with up to 2 decimals; null removes it
and the channel takes its default); `flat_rate` (present: the store's flat rate for every online channel, null
to move it to the channel rates); `delivery_courier` own | fleet (who delivers its Mini App delivery orders:
own delivery 10% or RIZQIM courier 15%); `reason`. Only new orders are affected: an order keeps the rate it was
placed with. Answers the commission block.

post.description:
`plan` (an active plan's code), `period` (monthly | yearly; yearly only on a v2 plan; for a store without a
subscription, which starts now with the plan's trial when it is its first), `immediately` (default false: the
change waits for the end of the month or the yearly term; a higher v2 plan applied now is prorated, a lower one
always waits), `reason`. Answers the store's billing.

`immediately` (true: it ends now and the month in progress is not billed; false: at the end of the month or of
the paid yearly term), `reason`. Months that already ended are billed first.

`period` monthly | yearly (v2 plans only), `reason`. During the trial it applies at once; otherwise monthly →
yearly from the next month (the yearly invoice is issued then) and yearly → monthly when the paid term ends.

`trial_ends_at` (a later moment, at most 90 days from now) or `days` (added to the current trial end), `reason`.
Only a subscription in its trial. The months the trial touches are not billed.

422.description: Not in its trial, too far or not later (billing_rule)

get.description:
Current subscriptions, newest first, cursor pages (`cursor`, `per_page` 1–100, default 30). Filters: `status`
(trialing, active, past_due, locked, cancelled — cancelled lists ended rows), `plan` (code), `period` (monthly,
yearly), `trial_ends_within` (days: trials ending in that many days), `store_id`. Each row: the subscription and
its store's name.

Cursor pages (`cursor` from `next_cursor`, `per_page` 1–100, default 30). `status`: open (default: new and in
progress, the oldest first), new, in_progress, answered, resolved, all (newest first). `assigned`: me, none or a
member id; `type` (WRONG_ITEM, ORDER_NOT_RECEIVED, QUALITY_ISSUE, COURIER_ISSUE, PAYMENT_ISSUE, OTHER); `waiting=1`:
only the ones waiting longer than `waiting_hours` (open, not answered by the store); `q`: the order's code or a
word of the text. `counts` per support status plus `open` and `waiting`; `assignees`: the members a complaint
can be given to; `types` and `statuses`: the words.

The row plus the full `description`, the `customer` (phone masked unless admin.pii.view; a reveal is audited;
`telegram_linked` says whether a reply can reach them), the `order`, `store_reply` (the store's own answer),
`replies` (what support sent), `resolution` (note, by, at), `history` (its audit trail) and `actions` (reply,
resolve, reopen).

patch.description:
`support_status` (new, in_progress, answered — `resolved` is the resolve action: 422 `use_resolve`) and/or
`assigned_to` (a team member with support.view, or null; 422 `assignee_invalid`). Moving to in_progress without
an assignee gives it to you; moving a resolved one back reopens it. Answers the card.

422.description: Resolve needs a note (use_resolve), or the assignee cannot take complaints (assignee_invalid)

post.description:
`text` (1–1000 characters, plain text) goes to the customer's Telegram through the RIZQIM bot, queued; kept in
the complaint's `replies`; the complaint becomes `answered` (and yours, if nobody had it). `canned_reply_id`: the
tayyor javob it started from (optional). 422 `no_recipient` (no Telegram), 503 `telegram_not_configured`, 409
`already_resolved`. Answers the card.

`note` (3–1000 characters): how it was solved. The complaint becomes `resolved`, and the store flow is closed
with the note as its resolution (the customer reads it in the Mini App). 409 `already_resolved`. Answers the card.

post.description:
Multipart or JSON: `store_id`, `kind` (debt_charge — debt up; debt_credit — commission debt down; debt_payment —
money received outside the top-up flow, pays the oldest invoices first; wallet_credit; wallet_debit — never
below zero, 422 `insufficient_wallet`), `amount` (so'm, more than 0, up to 2 decimals), `reason`, optional
`document` (pdf, jpg, png, webp; up to 10 MB). Under 1 000 000 so'm it is applied at once (`status: applied`);
from it, `pending` until another member approves it.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

422.description: The wallet cannot cover a wallet_debit (insufficient_wallet)

get.description: With `transactions` — the ledger rows it wrote once applied.

post.description:
A pending adjustment, by a member other than the one who made it (403 `four_eyes`, a superadmin too); its
ledger row is written now. `reason` required. Repeating it answers the same result; decided otherwise: 409
`adjustment_decided`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

403.description: The maker cannot approve it (four_eyes) or step-up needed (reauth_required)

get.description: The file as it was uploaded (private storage). 404 when it has none.

post.description: A pending adjustment (the one who made it may withdraw it this way); nothing is booked. `reason` required.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

get.description:
`filter`: all (the default), debt (owes anything), over_limit (the commission debt is over the credit limit —
Mini App orders are refused), subscription_debt (unpaid invoices), wallet (RIZQIM holds money for it); `q` — the
store's name. Largest first (debt; the wallet for `wallet`), pages of `per_page` (1–100, default 50). `totals`
— over all stores. Amounts are decimal strings; the commission debt is debt − subscription debt.

The row plus `breakdown` — "Hisoblangan — Ushlangan qarz — O'tkaziladi": `accrued` (asked for), `netted` (the
store's debt taken first) and `transfer` (to the card), `lines` (each invoice or the commission debt it closed,
with the ledger row). For an open payout it is what approving now would do (`preview: true`); `balances` —
the store's wallet and debt now; `actions`. The card number is full with admin.pii.view (audited), else masked.

post.description:
`reason` required. Under 1 000 000 so'm: pays it out now. From 1 000 000 so'm: the first approval is recorded
(`status: awaiting_second`), a different member's approval pays it out (403 `four_eyes` for the first approver,
a superadmin too). Paying out nets the store's debt first, then transfers the rest; 422 `insufficient_wallet`
when the wallet cannot cover the amount (nothing is booked). A decided payout: 409 `payout_decided`; the same
member repeating the approval gets the same answer and nothing runs twice (also with the same Idempotency-Key).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

403.description: The first approver cannot complete it (four_eyes) or step-up needed (reauth_required)

post.description: `reason` (why; the owner sees it as the resolution note) required. Open payouts only (409 `payout_decided`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

get.description:
`period` — "YYYY-MM", an Asia/Tashkent month (default: the current one). Commission: the orders delivered in
the month that are still delivered, less what partial refunds took back; by channel (`unknown` — orders from
before the channel was recorded). Subscriptions: the month's invoices that are not void. Stores — largest total
first. Amounts are decimal strings.

The same report as an .xlsx workbook ("Umumiy" and "Ovqatxonalar" sheets). Needs admin.export as well; each
export is recorded in the audit log.

Delivered orders whose ledger booking (commission, the store's money, the referral reward) failed and is retried
every 10 minutes (RetryFailedSettlementsJob) until `max_attempts`; `gave_up` — the automatic retries stopped.
Oldest first.

post.description:
Books the order again now through the same path as the automatic retries (also after they gave up). `reason`
required. `booked` — whether it is booked now; a failure stays on the list with its new error (its attempts
go up). An order booked or refunded meanwhile is cleared (`booked: false`, `order: null`). 404 for an order
without a failed booking.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

get.description:
`ledger`: debt (the debt ledger: commission, top-ups, netting, subscription invoices, refunds, adjustments; the
default) or wallet (settlements, payouts, refunds, adjustments). Newest first, cursor pages (`per_page` 1–100,
default 50). Card numbers in notes are masked. A netting row names what it closed (`subscription_invoice`),
a payout's rows carry `payout_request_id`.

The counts behind the tabs and the second-approval queue: open payouts (`pending` — no approval yet,
`awaiting_second`), adjustments waiting for a second approval, settlement failures (and how many gave up), stuck
top-ups, stores over their credit limit, the store totals; `threshold` — from this amount two members approve.

Owners' Click and Payme top-ups of their debt: `status` (pending, paid, cancelled, all — the default),
`provider` (click, payme), `store_id`, `stuck=1` — pending for more than 30 minutes in the last 3 days (the owner
left the payment page, or the provider's callback never came: check the provider's cabinet). Newest first,
cursor pages. `transaction_id` — the debt ledger row a paid one wrote.

Pages (`page`, `per_page` 1-100, default 30), the least healthy first. Filters: `status` (configuring, active,
paused, disconnected), `provider` (iiko, alipos, yandex_eats, uzum_tezkor, partner_api, ...), `direction`
(rizqim_to_pos, aggregator_to_rizqim), `mode` (sandbox, production), `health` (good: score 80+, attention: 50-79,
disconnected: under 50, unknown: no score yet), `store_id`, `q` (store or branch name). `counts` ignore the
filters. Empty until phase 5 connects the first system.

The list row plus `credentials` (key names, `configured`, `last4`: the last 4 characters of a credential of 16 or more, only with `admin.integrations.manage`, else null), `settings` (secret-looking keys
"[redacted]", phones masked), the last 10 events, the menu map counts (`external_refs` by type) and how many of
its orders are stuck.

post.description:
`reason`. Nothing is sent to or taken from the outside system while it is paused (phase 5 adapters check it).
Pausing a paused one changes nothing. Answers the card.
`reason`. Back to the status it had before the pause. Resuming one that is not paused changes nothing.

Newest first, by cursor (`cursor` from `next_cursor`, `per_page` 1-100, default 25). Filters: `connection` (uuid),
`store_id`, `status` (pending, sent, acknowledged, failed, dead), `type` (order.push, menu.sync, webhook.status,
...), `direction` (inbound, outbound), `from` / `to` (Y-m-d, Tashkent). The rows have no bodies; the event does.

The row plus the idempotency key, the signature check, the last attempt and the request and response bodies
(keys that look secret "[redacted]", phone numbers masked).

Orders pushed to an outside POS and not confirmed for 2 minutes while still open, the oldest first (at most
100; `count` is all of them). Empty until phase 5.

Every category (top-level and inner) in the Mini App's order (`sort_order`), with its product and sub-category
counts. `is_active` false = hidden from the catalog (its products stay). `image_preview` is the admin path of the
icon (GET, same session), `image_url` its public URL.

post.description:
multipart/form-data: `name` (2-255), `parent_id` (a top-level category; empty = top-level itself), `image` (the
icon: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 4 MB, optional), `is_active` (1/0, default 1), `reason`. It goes to the end of the
list. Answers the row (201). 422 `invalid_parent`.

422.description: A rule refused it (invalid_parent) or a field is wrong

put.description:
`ids`: every category id, once, in the new order (the whole list; one that is out of date is refused with 409
`order_stale`), and `reason`. Answers the list.

post.description:
POST (multipart/form-data or JSON). Any of `name`, `parent_id` (empty = top-level; a category with sub-categories
cannot become one), `is_active` (hide or show), `image` (a new icon replaces the old one), `remove_image` (1:
drop the icon), and `reason` (required). Answers the row.

422.description: A rule refused it (invalid_parent) or a field is wrong

delete.description:
Only one with no products and no sub-categories (409 `category_in_use` otherwise: hide it instead). Needs a
step-up and a `reason`. Answers `{id}`.

get.description: The stored icon (JPEG, PNG or WebP) for the admin screens. 404 `no_image` when there is none.

Pages (`page`, `per_page` 1-100, default 30). Filters: `q` (part of the code), `status` (active, inactive,
expired, exhausted), `store_id` (codes tied to that store). `sort`: newest (default), code, expiry. Money as
decimal strings; `value` is a percent for `percentage` codes and so'm for `fixed` ones.

`stats` counts the orders that use the code and are still standing (not cancelled, rejected or refunded, the
same orders the limits count): `uses`, `unique_customers`, `discount_total` (so'm given away) and `gmv` (the
orders' totals after the discount). `locked`: some order carries the code, so its value can no longer change.

post.description:
`code` (3-50 letters, digits, `-` or `_`; stored upper case, one per code), `type` (`percentage` or `fixed`),
`value` (percentage: above 0, up to 100, two decimals; fixed: whole so'm above 0), `min_order_amount` (so'm,
default 0), `max_discount_amount` (a cap in so'm, only for `percentage`; ignored for `fixed`), `usage_limit`
(total uses, empty = unlimited), `per_user_limit` (uses per customer, empty = unlimited), `store_id` (empty = every
store), `is_active` (default true), `expires_at` (ISO 8601, in the future, empty = never), `reason`. Answers the
row (201). 422 `invalid_value` when the value does not fit the type.

422.description: A rule refused it (invalid_value) or a field is wrong

get.description:
The row and `recent_orders`: the last 10 orders that carry the code (uuid for the order card, status, discount
and total as decimal strings).

delete.description:
Only a code no order ever carried; a used one is switched off instead (409 `promo_code_used`). Needs a step-up and
a `reason`. Answers `{id}`.

patch.description:
Any field of the new code, and `reason` (required). Once an order carries the code, `code`, `type`, `value`,
`max_discount_amount` and `store_id` cannot change: 422 `promo_code_used` with `data.fields` (create a new code
and switch the old one off). The limits, `min_order_amount`, `expires_at` and `is_active` stay editable.

422.description: The code was used (promo_code_used) or a field is wrong

post.description: `reason` required. Answers the card.

The code stops working at once (the order flow checks it on every order); orders already placed keep it.
`reason` required. Answers the card.

get.description:
Every banner in the Mini App's order (`sort_order`), at most 200. Filters: `status` (live, scheduled, ended,
inactive), `q` (part of the title). `status` is computed now (Asia/Tashkent): inactive = switched off; scheduled =
`starts_at` still ahead; ended = `ends_at` passed; live = what the Mini App shows. `image_preview` is the admin
path of the image (GET, same session), `image_url` the public URL the Mini App uses.

post.description:
multipart/form-data: `title` (2-255), `image` (JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 4 MB, required), `store_id` and/or
`product_id` (what a tap opens; a product must belong to the store when both are given), `is_active` (1/0,
default 1), `starts_at` / `ends_at` (ISO 8601, `ends_at` after `starts_at`, else 422 `invalid_schedule`; both empty = always), `reason`. It
goes to the end of the row. Answers the banner (201).

422.description: A rule refused it (product_store_mismatch, invalid_schedule) or a field is wrong

put.description:
`ids`: every banner id, once, in the new order (the whole row; a list that is out of date is refused with 409
`order_stale` so nobody overwrites a colleague's order), and `reason`. Answers the list.

get.description:
The banners the home screen lists right now, in its order: the same query as `GET /catalog` without a store
(switched on and inside their schedule). `image_preview` as in the list.

post.description:
POST (multipart/form-data or JSON; PHP does not read a multipart PATCH). Any of `title`, `image` (a new file
replaces the old one), `store_id`, `product_id` (empty clears), `is_active`, `starts_at`, `ends_at` (empty clears),
and `reason` (required). Answers the banner.

delete.description:
Needs a step-up and a `reason`. The banner and its stored image go; the audit entry keeps its fields. Answers
`{id}`.

get.description:
The stored image itself (JPEG, PNG or WebP) for the admin screens, which cannot load the public storage URL.
404 `no_image` when there is none (or it is an outside URL).

`months` — how many months back (3–24, default 12; the last one is the month in progress, `partial: true`).
`cards`: `mrr` (monthly recurring revenue now: active subscriptions' monthly price, a yearly one divided by 12,
extra terminals included, trials left out) with `mrr_change` against the start of the month, `arr` (= MRR × 12),
`paying_stores`, `trialing_stores`, `arpa` (MRR per paying store), `active_stores`, `churn_rate` of the latest
finished month (`churn_month`), `gmv_month` and `commission_month` of the month so far. `series`: per month the
MRR at its end, paying, trialing and active stores. `movement`: per month `opening` → `new` / `expansion` /
`contraction` / `churned` (`mrr` and the number of `stores`) → `closing`. `churn`: per month the stores active at
the start, how many churned (went inactive, or their subscription ended), `rate` and `revenue_rate` in percent.
`revenue`: per month marketplace `orders`, `gmv`, `commission` and paid subscription invoices from the Bugun
aggregate, with `missing_days` / `complete` when the aggregate lacks days. Money is a decimal string. Cached a few
minutes (`generated_at`); `refresh=1` rebuilds it, at most once a minute per member (sooner: the cached report).

Store applications created in the last `months` months (3–24, default 12) by pipeline stage: `reached` — how many
got to the stage or further, `share` of all applications in percent, `median_days` spent in the stage before
moving on (null while nobody has). Totals: `applications`, `active`, `rejected`, `open`, `conversion` (active ÷
all, percent) and `median_days_to_active`. Stage moves are read from the audit log.

`state`: `active` (default: open and acknowledged together), `open`, `acknowledged`, `resolved` or `all`.
Unresolved alerts come whole (up to 200): open before acknowledged, critical before warning, newest first. With
`resolved` or `all` the history is paged, newest first (`cursor` from `next_cursor`, `per_page` 1–100, default
25). Filters: `kind`, `severity`, `store_id`. `counts`: open, acknowledged and resolved in the last 7 days.

post.description:
"I am on it": the alert leaves the Bugun attention list and stays open for everyone else with the member's name
on it. Optional `note` (up to 500 characters). Only an `open` alert can be acknowledged (409 `alert_not_open`).

409.description: The alert is not open any more (alert_not_open)

post.description:
Marks it done by hand; optional `note`. If the problem is still there the next minute's check opens a new alert.
The ops group is told (when its open message went out). 409 `alert_resolved` if it is already resolved.

get.description:
Newest first, cursor pages (`cursor` from `next_cursor`, `per_page` 1–100, default 25). Each row: the job's short
name and class, queue, the exception's first line (redacted) and when it failed. Filters: `queue`, `q` (part of
the job class name), `from` / `to` (dates, inclusive). `total` counts all failed jobs.

The full exception text with the stack trace and the job's payload as plain data, both redacted: keys that hold
secrets (tokens, passwords, codes, keys, card data) show `[redacted]`, tokens and phone numbers inside text are
masked. The job is read without running any of its code. The exception beyond its first line and the payload's
data (the serialized job: texts, names, addresses) are returned only to members with `admin.monitoring.manage`
or `admin.pii.view`; everyone else gets `details_hidden: true`, the job class, queue and the first line.

delete.description:
Removes it for good. Needs step-up and a `reason`; the audit entry keeps the job name, queue and uuid, not the
payload.

post.description:
Puts the job back on its queue with its attempts reset and removes it from the list (like
`php artisan queue:retry`). Optional `reason`. 404 if it is no longer there (retried or deleted meanwhile).

get.description:
`status` is `ok`, `degraded` (the app works, something needs a look: a stale scheduler, a long queue, Reverb
down, an old backup) or `fail` (database or Redis). `database`, `redis`, `queue` (the `/health` report's numbers
plus every queue with its size and the age of its oldest waiting job, and failed job counts) and `scheduler` come
from the same report as `GET /health`. `reverb`: `ok`, `fail` or `not_configured` (real-time is switched off).
`backup`: `ok`, `stale` (older than the backup rule's hours) or `missing` (the backup service never reported).
`app` (version, commit), `sentry` (`configured`, link to the project from the config; no Sentry API calls) and
`alerts` (open, acknowledged, critical unresolved counts).

One rule per kind (failed_jobs_spike, queue_backlog, pos_device_offline, fiscal_failures, settlement_failures,
backup_stale, scheduler_stale). `fields` says what each threshold means (label, unit, allowed range) and is null
for a threshold the kind does not use; `defaults` are the built-in values. `telegram_configured`: whether an ops
(or superadmin) chat is set, i.e. whether `telegram: true` reaches anyone.

put.description:
Any of `enabled`, `telegram`, `threshold`, `threshold_secondary`, `window_minutes` (only the thresholds the kind
uses, within its range: see `fields` in the list) plus a required `reason`. Switching a rule off resolves its
alerts. Needs step-up. Answers with all the rules.

422.description: Value outside the kind's range, or a threshold the kind does not use

get.description:
Newest first, cursor pages (`cursor` from `next_cursor`, `per_page` 1–100, default 30). Filters: `status` — a
status group: `active` (not finished), `new`, `kitchen` (accepted, preparing, ready), `en_route` (courier
assigned, on the way), `done` (delivered, refunded), `canceled` (canceled, rejected); `channel` (telegram,
mobile); `region_id` (the branch's region); `store_id`; `sla` — `late` or `warning` (the running
stage at 80–100% of its limit); `from` / `to` (dates in Asia/Tashkent, inclusive); `q` — the short code (with or
without #), the start of the uuid, or the customer's phone: 4+ of its digits with admin.pii.view, otherwise only
the whole number (+998 and nine digits, or the nine digits). `counts` has every group under the same filters
(done and canceled count today only when no from/to is given). `sla` on each row: null when no stage runs
(waiting for an online payment, ready, with a courier not yet on the way, finished). `manual_refund_required`:
a cancelled, rejected or refunded order with money still to give back (`refunds.refundable` > 0 on the card).

Minutes for each stage: `accept` (checkout → accepted), `prepare` (accepted → ready), `deliver` (on the way →
delivered); `warning_ratio` — a stage is "warning" from this share of its limit, "late" from the limit.

put.description:
Any of `accept` (1–120), `prepare` (5–300), `deliver` (5–300) minutes, and `reason`. admin.system.manage and a
step-up. Takes effect at once: the list, the attention rows and the next watcher run use the new limits.

get.description:
Per store: `orders` that reached the store (not an unpaid online order, not one the customer cancelled while new),
`acceptance_rate` (0–1), `avg_accept_minutes` (cash and keshbek orders, checkout → accepted by staff),
`avg_prep_minutes` (accepted → ready), `cancel_rate` (0–1), the store's `rating` and the ratings given in the
period. With `store_id`: that store; without: up to 50 stores with orders in the period, the weakest first.
Cached 5 minutes.

Everything about one marketplace order: status history with who did it, items, totals, payments and refund
requests (`refunds.refundable` = paid − refunded), courier, customer, store and branch (phones masked unless
admin.pii.view; every reveal is audited), fiscal receipts, the running SLA, the SLA timeline per stage and the
recorded SLA crossings, the audit entries about the order, and `actions` — what this member may do now.

post.description:
`cancel_reason`: one of the store-side reasons (customer_request, no_show — a pickup order already accepted only,
out_of_stock, store_closed, courier_unavailable, other); `note` (optional, the customer sees it); `reason` (the
team's own, in the audit log and the status history). Paid money follows the cancel rules: keshbek goes back to
the balance, Click/Payme (or collected cash) is flagged for a manual refund — ask for it with a refund request.
The store hears about it in its order chats. Answers the order card.

422.description: Cannot be cancelled now (illegal, stale) or the reason does not apply (reason)

post.description:
`to`: `store` (the store's order chats: its admin chat and the managers who get order cards) or `customer` (the
RIZQIM bot); `text` (1–1000 characters, sent as plain text); `reason`. Queued like every Telegram message. 422
`no_recipient` when there is nobody to send it to; 503 `telegram_not_configured` without the bot.
post.summary: Message the store or the customer

post.description:
`amount` (so'm, up to 2 decimals; more than 0 and at most the card's `refunds.refundable`: paid − refunded) and
`reason`. Only for a finished order (delivered, canceled, rejected, refunded: 422 `order_active` otherwise), one
pending request per order (409 `refund_request_pending`). The request waits for another member's approval.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

422.description: Too much (amount_exceeds_refundable, data.refundable) or the order is still in progress (order_active)

post.description:
`status`: a status the lifecycle allows from the current one (the card's `actions.transitions`), never canceled
or rejected (use cancel) nor refunded (use a refund request). There is no forced move: anything else is 422
`illegal`. `courier_id` (optional) for a move to a courier: one of the store's couriers; without it the least
busy one is picked, as for the store. `reason` is required. Answers the order card.

422.description: Not allowed from the current status (illegal, stale, use_cancel, use_refund_request) or no courier (courier)

get.description:
Pages (`page`, `per_page` 1-100, default 30), the longest unseen first. Filters: `state` (online: seen in the last
10 minutes; offline; never: never seen; revoked; all; without it, every device that is not revoked), `type`
(pos, kds, partner_mobile, courier, ...), `terminal=1` (kassa and KDS only), `store_id`, `outdated=1` (an older app
version than the newest seen on an active device of the same type), `q` (device or store name, uuid start). Each row
has `state`, `latest_version`, `outdated` and the offline queue the till last reported. `counts` and
`latest_versions` ignore the filters.
The same row as in the list, by the device's uuid (the Bugun links open it).

post.description:
`reason`. The device and everything signed in on it stops working at once; a terminal has to be paired again with
a new code by the owner. Revoking a revoked device changes nothing. Answers the device.

get.description:
Newest first, pages (`page`, `per_page` 1-100, default 30). Filters: `status` (open: failed or pending, the
default; failed; pending; issued; all), `driver` (the fiscal provider asked: sandbox, null, ..., external — a
receipt Payme/Click registered), `store_id`, `from` / `to` (dates in Asia/Tashkent), `q` (uuid start or receipt
number). `summary`: open failed and pending receipts in all and per provider (`by_driver`, with the latest error).
`error` is the provider's reason, cut to 300 characters.

The row, the whole error, the lines and payments as they were sent and the fiscal sign once registered. The
provider's raw answer is not shown.

post.description:
`reason`. A pending or failed receipt is sent to the provider at once (a failed one becomes pending first). The
answer is the receipt afterwards; it stays failed or pending when the provider still refuses (the message says
why). An issued receipt, or one recorded from Payme/Click: 422 `already_issued`.

get.description:
Newest first, pages (`page`, `per_page` 1-100, default 30). Filters: `status` (issued, paid, void, or `overdue`:
unpaid after the due date, Asia/Tashkent), `store_id`, `period` (YYYY-MM), `dunning` (the latest reminder step:
reminder_1, reminder_3, reminder_7, locked, unlocked), `q` (part of the number). Rows carry the days overdue and
the latest dunning step. `counts`: issued / overdue / paid / void invoices and the unpaid sum (not filtered).

The invoice with its lines, paid and outstanding parts and every dunning step, and the store's debt split
(subscription part and commission part).

post.description:
`reason`. Only an unpaid invoice: a paid or partly paid one is refused (422 `invoice_paid`; money goes back by a
manual adjustment). The invoice no longer counts as income and its amount comes off the store's debt (a reversal
row in the ledger). From 1 000 000 so'm (`config('finance.four_eyes_threshold')`) two members: the first call is a
request (the invoice stays `issued`, `invoice.void_request` shows who asked, audited as
`admin.pos.invoice_void_requested`), the same member again changes nothing, a different member's call voids it.
Voiding one again changes nothing.

422.description: A paid or partly paid invoice (invoice_paid)

get.description:
`subscriptions` (current subscriptions per status, `trial_ending`: trials ending in 3 days), `invoices` (issued,
overdue, paid, void counts and the `outstanding` sum of the unpaid ones), `devices` (active devices: online,
offline, never seen, outdated, per type; revoked), `shifts` (the last 30 days: closed with a cash difference,
force-closed, open), `fiscal` (failed and pending receipts and `by_driver`: per fiscal provider) and
`sync_errors` (offline operations nobody resolved). A group the member may not see is null.

Newest first, pages (`page`, `per_page` 1-100, default 30). Filters: `kind` (difference: closed with a cash
difference, counted minus expected, so a negative one is missing cash; force_closed; open), `store_id`, `from` /
`to` (business dates, YYYY-MM-DD). `counts` per kind under the other filters.

The row, the banknotes counted, the Z report as kept at closing (`summary`), who forced the close and the cash
movements (in and out of the drawer).

Newest first, pages (`page`, `per_page` 1-100, default 30). Filters: `state` (open: nobody resolved it, the
default; resolved; all), `status` (rejected: not applied; conflict: applied with a difference), `type` (the
operation, e.g. bill.pay), `store_id`, `device` (uuid), `from` / `to` (dates in Asia/Tashkent). Rows carry no
payload (the card has it). `counts`: open rejected / conflicting operations.

The row, the payload the till sent (keys that look like a phone, card, PIN or secret are replaced by ***) and what
the server made of it (`refs`). By the operation's id.

post.description:
`resolution`: `resolved` (somebody did what was needed by hand) or `dismissed` (nothing to do); `reason` is kept
as the resolution note. A resolved rejected operation no longer keeps its till's shift from closing. Resolving
one again changes nothing. Answers the card.

get.description:
For the approval queue: `status` (pending — the default —, approved, rejected, all), `store_id`; newest first,
cursor pages (`per_page` 1–100, default 30). Each with its order (uuid, short code, store, status, total).

post.description:
By a member other than the one who asked (403 `four_eyes`). Runs the refund: a delivered order refunded in full
with nothing of it given back before becomes `refunded` (commission and settlement reversed, keshbek back to the
balance; mode `order_refunded`); otherwise (a part, the rest after a part, a cancelled order) the amount is
spread over the payments still paid (`execution.allocations`): a keshbek share goes back to the customer's
balance at once, exactly that amount (mode `balance` when all of it did), any other share is a manual refund
(mode `manual`). `execution.manual_amount` is what the approver returns by hand in the provider's cabinet or in
cash (no provider refund API is called). The amount is checked again against what is refundable now (a payment
the provider refunded since counts in full): 422 `amount_exceeds_refundable`. `reason` required.
Idempotent: a repeat (or the same Idempotency-Key) answers the same result; a request already decided otherwise
is 409 `refund_request_decided`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

403.description: The requester cannot decide (four_eyes) or step-up needed (reauth_required)

post.description:
By a member other than the one who asked (403 `four_eyes`); `reason` (why) is required. A repeat answers the
same result.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional: a new UUID per action, the same one when retrying it; a repeat returns the first answer.

get.description:
`roles` in display order (`editable`: false for superadmin), `permissions` with their section (`group`),
`grants`: role => the permissions it holds now, and `defaults`: role => the built-in set before the
superadmin's changes (a cell differing from it is "O'zgartirilgan"; PUT with `allowed: null` resets it).

put.description:
`allowed`: true grants, false takes away, null resets to the role's default. Only a superadmin changes the
matrix (403 `superadmin_only` for any other team.manage holder). The superadmin role cannot be changed (422
`role_not_editable`). Needs step-up. Answers with the whole matrix.

422.description: Superadmin is fixed (role_not_editable) or invalid input

get.description:
`q` at least 2 characters. Each hit: `type` (store, order, user, member), `id`, `title`, `subtitle` and `href`,
the admin app path to open (`/stores/{id}`, `/orders/{uuid}`, `/users/{id}`, `/team/{id}`). Types the member
has no permission for (stores.view, orders.view, users.view, team.manage) are left out. By phone: with
admin.pii.view any 4+ digits of the number (each number shown is an audited reveal); without it only the whole
number (`+998901234567`, `90 123 45 67`...).

Filters: `stage` (a stage, `open` — every stage but active and rejected — or `overdue`: open and past the due
date), `assignee_id` (or `me`), `source`, `q` (name, owner, the whole phone); pages (`page`, `per_page` 1–200,
default 50), the overdue first, then by due date. `stage_counts`: per stage under the same filters (but stage),
plus `overdue`. `stages`: the pipeline with labels.

post.description:
The public form's fields (`name`, `format`, `region_id`, `city`, `owner_name`, `phone`, `tin`, `comment`) and
optionally `assignee_id` and `due_on`. Source `admin`. 201 with the card.
post.summary: Add an application (typed in by the team)

get.description:
The row fields and `phone` (masked unless admin.pii.view, reveals audited), `tin`, `comment`, the rejection,
`checklist` (every stage: items with `done`, `ticked` by hand, `detected` from the store), `crm` (notes, tasks),
`audit` and `actions`.

patch.description:
Any of the fields, `assignee_id` (a team member with admin.stores.manage, or null), `due_on` (the current stage's
deadline). Answers the card.

post.description:
`item` (a key of any stage's checklist), `done` (true / false). Detected items are done whatever is ticked.
Answers the card.

The store, its owner (a vouched SMS login phone and a Telegram invite) and the main branch, through the same
path as every other store creation (StoreProvisioner). Store `pending` and hidden from the marketplace until the application
reaches `faol`. Fields: `branch_district_id`, `branch_address`, `branch_lat`, `branch_lng` (required);
`branch_region_id` (default: the application's region), `branch_radius` (5), `branch_phone`,
`branch_open_time`/`branch_close_time` (HH:MM), `name`, `owner_name`, `owner_phone` (+998XXXXXXXXX; default: the
application's), `phone`, `tin`, `legal_name`, `commission_rate` (a flat rate; none: the channel rates of Billing v2),
`payment_account_type`; `reason`. Step-up.
409 `already_converted`, 409 `owner_phone_taken` (another staff account has it), 422 `owner_phone_invalid`.
Answers the card and `invite_link` (only here).
post.summary: Create the store from the application

409.description: Already converted or the phone is taken (already_converted, owner_phone_taken)

post.description: `body` (1–2000 characters). 201 with the note.
post.summary: Add a note to an application

post.description:
`reason` (the team sees it on the card). A converted application's store becomes `rejected` and hidden. Step-up.
409 `already_rejected`, 422 `already_active`. Answers the card.

`stage` (not `rejected`: use reject), `note` (optional), `due_on` (optional; default today + the stage's days).
Forward needs the required checklist items of every stage passed (422 `checklist_incomplete` with `stage` and
`missing`); `menu` and later need the store (422 `store_required`); `active` activates the store and needs a

Prices, stock, the promo code and the delivery fee are checked on the server. `payment_url` is set for online
payment methods (Click, Payme): open it to pay; the order is cancelled when it stays unpaid. 400 with the reason
when the order cannot be placed (store closed, item unavailable, minimum not reached...).

P1-21 (docs/MENU.md): `items.*.quantity` may be a fraction for items sold by weight (kg/l, at least
`min_quantity`, in `quantity_step` steps); `items.*.modifiers` lists the chosen modifiers as uuids or
`{id: uuid, quantity}`; prices always come from the server. 422 when a modifier rule is broken, the item is on
the branch's stop-list, its batch is sold out ("tugadi") or it is hidden on the channel. The channel is decided by
the server from the sign-in (P1-34): `mobile` for a token of a customer mobile app device, else `telegram`; a
`channel` in the body is accepted for older apps but ignored. `type=dine_in` is refused with 422 (hall orders
are taken by staff on the POS). An `Idempotency-Key` header makes retries safe: the same key with the same body
within 24 hours returns the first response (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`), with another body 409.

(`pos_takeaway`). `guests_count` (hall: at least 1) drives the per-guest charges and the automatic "choy-non"
lines. `items` (optional) is the first round; `send: true` sends its `now` lines to the kitchen at once.
`external_id`: the device's own id for the order; a repeat returns the same order. A room with an open order is
422 `table_occupied`; a closed zone or inactive place 422 `table_inactive`. Needs orders.manage.

A new online order (Telegram, mobile, aggregator) of the branch is accepted at the till: `new` → `accepted`
(the customer is told, the kitchen gets it). Accepted already: 200 unchanged. Not new any more (rejected,
cancelled): 422. A POS order: 422 `not_online_order`. Optional `version` (409 when stale). Needs orders.manage.

The order's billing state (`billed_amount`, `paid_amount`, `unbilled_amount`: what no bill carries yet, e.g. a
round added after the bill was printed; `fiscal_pending`: a bill is paid but its receipt is not issued yet,
"fiskal kutmoqda"; `bills_out_of_date`: the order changed after its open bills were made: bill again), its bills
(void ones only with `all=1`) with their lines, charges, per-guest amount and payments, and its refunds. Needs
orders.view in the order's branch.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Include voided bills.

post.description:
Bills what is left to bill of the order (bills already being paid stay; other open or printed bills are voided
and made again). `mode`: `single` (one bill), `equal` (`parts` bills with the same total; the remainder tiyin on
the first), `items` (`bills`: each with its `items` — `order_item_id` and `quantity`, fractions too, e.g. 0.5 of
1.5 kg; every line left must be given out in full; optional `guests` for the per-guest amount). The discount and
the charges (room fee, minimum spend top-up, service charge, place fee) are shared in proportion; all shares are
exact to the tiyin. `version`: the order's (409 `version_conflict` when stale). One bill: orders.manage or
pos.take_payment; splitting: pos.take_payment (403 `permission_denied`). A waiter bills only their own orders
(another waiter's: a manager's `approval_token` for orders.manage, else 403 `approval_required`). 409
`nothing_to_bill`, `order_closed`,
`not_pos_order`; 422 `items_not_covered`, `bill_empty`, `item_not_billable`, `parts_invalid`.

`reason` is required. orders.cancel, or a manager's one-time `approval_token` for orders.cancel (POST
/pos/approvals; 403 `approval_required`). An order with a payment is refused: 409 `has_payments` (refund the
payments first, POST /pos/refunds). Every line still on the order is voided — lines already sent get a kitchen
void ("O'CHIRILDI"), unsent lines give their stock and kazan portion back — open or printed bills are voided, the
order becomes `canceled` and its table free; a booking's order completes the booking (its deposits stay
`taken`, to refund or retain). Audited; the owner is alerted. P3-37: a closed order whose every payment was
refunded in full (`payment_status` refunded) is cancelled too, with the same permission: it becomes `canceled`,
keeps `closed_at`, its lines and paid bills stay, no receipt is issued (the refund receipts already reverse the
sale). Any other closed or cancelled order: 422 `order_closed`. 409 `version_conflict`.

post.description:
P3-37. `kind` `percent` (`value` 0 < v ≤ 100, two decimals) or `amount` (`value` in so'm, 0 < v ≤ the dishes'
subtotal); `value` 0 takes the discount off. `reason` is required unless `value` is 0 (up to 255). The
discount is on the dishes (`charges.items_subtotal`), before the service charge; `discount` is its amount in
whole so'm (half-up). A percent stays a percent: adding or voiding lines works it out again; an amount never
exceeds the dishes. Who: orders.discount — any discount; a cashier (pos.take_payment) up to the branch's
`pos_settings.cashier_discount_max_percent` (an amount by its percent of the dishes), while no bill was printed;
otherwise 403 `approval_required` (`permission: orders.discount`): send a manager's one-time `approval_token`
for orders.discount (POST /pos/approvals). Taking a discount off needs orders.manage only. The waiter rule
applies. 409 `paid_bill_affected` once a bill of the order has a payment or is paid (refund first); 409
`version_conflict`; 422 `order_closed`; 422 validation (`value` above the dishes, `reason` missing). A printed
bill no longer matches: bill again (POST /pos/orders/{uuid}/bills). Audited (`pos.order.discount`, old and
new); the owner is alerted at `pos_settings.alerts.discount_percent` and above; `order.items_changed` with
`change: charges_changed`. Not available offline (no sync operation).

by waiter (with the service charge their bills brought), discounts, voided lines, refunds, deposits taken and
applied, sales on credit and repayments, the drawer's movements and the expected cash. A closed shift: as at its

post.description:
Up to 50 operations of this till in its `seq` order, each with a new `op_id` (UUID; the same one when sent again:
it is applied once), `type` (order.open, order.round, order.send, order.void, order.served, bill.create, bill.pay,
order.close), `occurred_at` (the device's clock), `staff_id` (who did it: signed in on this till before the
outage, with the permission) and `payload`. Each result: `status` applied | conflict (applied, but a manager
should look: oversold, payment on a cancelled order, amount mismatch, stale menu, a taken room, a device price the
dish never had — `offline_price_mismatch`, the server's price applied) | rejected (not applied: "Sinxronlash
     * xatolari"; `invalid_payload` for content the server cannot store), `reason`, `message` and `refs` (the server's
order uuid and version, local number, line ids, bill and payment uuids, flags). `sent_at` (the device's clock now)
gives the clock skew: more than 5 minutes is `clock_warning` (and corrects the operations' times, kept within the
last 48 hours). `stopped_at`: a temporary database failure only. `queue` (size, oldest_at) is what is still in the device's queue including
this batch: the shift does not close while it is not empty. Only a POS terminal's own token.

post.description:
The line is ready (kitchen.manage). The first bump of an accepted order starts it (preparing). When every line is
ready a delivery or pickup order becomes ready by itself; a hall order (dine_in) stays preparing until it is
closed. P2-33: a courier_assigned order (a courier was assigned while it was cooking) takes bumps too, with no
status move. 422 when the order is not in the kitchen (new, ready, on its way, finished). Bumping a ready line
again answers 200 unchanged. P3-26: a held pre-order line with a due time (fire_mode hold, `due_at`, not sent yet)
may be bumped before the till sends it — ready implies sent: it gets its station and `sent_at` now and the POS
order's version moves. Returns the ticket.

Undo a mistaken bump: the line is back to pending (kitchen.manage). While the order is accepted or preparing,
and (P2-30) while it is ready but not yet with a courier or handed over: the order goes back to preparing
(`order.status_changed` and the history say so). P2-33: while a courier is assigned (courier_assigned) the line
is recalled with no status move. 422 once it is on its way or finished. Returns the ticket.

By permission (docs/AUTH.md §6): orders.manage (owner, manager, cashier, waiter) accepts, starts, marks ready and
hands over (pickup, hall: delivered); a cook (kitchen.manage) only starts cooking (accepted → preparing) and marks
ready (preparing → ready); cancelling or rejecting needs orders.cancel and a `reason`. The order's state machine
decides what can follow what (422 otherwise). Couriers are assigned with POST /orders/{uuid}/assign-courier.
Marking an order ready marks all its lines ready in the kitchen. The same status again answers 200 unchanged.
P2-30: `on_the_way` (the assigned courier picked the order up: courier_assigned → on_the_way) with
orders.assign_courier; an order without an assigned courier is a 422 (assign one first).

per IP address (429); a phone is taken once a day, however many requests name it. Answers 201 without any data about the application.

The terminal revokes itself with its own token (`auth:device`), e.g. before the kitchen display forgets its
pairing: the same as the owner's `POST /owner/devices/{uuid}/revoke` — the device is revoked, its token and every
staff PIN session on it stop working at once, and the audit log records `device.revoked` (`self_revoked: true`).
Pairing again needs a new code. Calling it again with the old token: 401.

P2-30: `role` (comma-separated, e.g. `cook,manager,owner` on a kitchen display) lists only those roles; an
unknown role: 422.
get.summary: GET /terminal/staff: who can sign in on this terminal (name, role, staff code), for the PIN pad

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Comma-separated roles to list: owner, manager, cashier, waiter, cook.

admin.description: Boshqaruv markazi sessiyasi (email + parol + 2FA, `POST /admin/auth/2fa/verify`): `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Faqat `/admin/*` uchun.

sanctum.description: Laravel Sanctum shaxsiy kirish tokeni: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

AdminPermission.description: P4-11: what a RIZQIM team member may do in the Boshqaruv markazi (admin API /api/v1/admin, `admin.can:` middleware). Separate from the store-level App\Enums\Permission: an admin permission never lets anyone act inside a store as its staff. Defaults per platform role: App\Services\Admin\PlatformRolePermissions; the superadmin may change them. Stage B sections (Bugun, Buyurtmalar, Monitoring...) use the entries that are already here.
AdminPermission.title: AdminPermission

BillStatus.description: order_bills.status: `open` when made, `printed` once handed to the guest (the order is locked from then on), `paid` when its payments cover it AND its sale receipt is issued, `void` when the order was billed again or cancelled.
BillStatus.title: BillStatus

BillingPeriod.description: P4-21: how often a subscription pays its base fee. Monthly: each month is billed when it ends. Yearly: 12 billing months are billed in advance when the term starts, for config('billing.yearly_months_charged') months' price; extra devices are still billed monthly when each month ends (docs/BILLING.md, "Yillik davr").
BillingPeriod.title: BillingPeriod

BookingEventType.description: What the booking is for (research report §3): helps the kitchen and the owner see the load ahead.
BookingEventType.title: BookingEventType

BookingPaymentStatus.description: A deposit: `taken` (an ADVANCE receipt was issued; part of it may already be offset, see applied_amount), `applied` (fully offset against the order's bills), `refunded` (what was left went back to the guest) or `retained` (what was left was kept after a cancellation or no-show, with a manager's approval).
BookingPaymentStatus.title: BookingPaymentStatus

BookingSource.description: Where the booking came from (choyxonas book by phone; Telegram and Instagram messages; a guest booking in person).
BookingSource.title: BookingSource

BookingStatus.description: A booking's life (research report §4): requested → confirmed → arrived (the order is open) → completed (the order is closed); requested or confirmed → canceled; confirmed → no_show; requested → arrived for a guest who came before the request was confirmed. A taken deposit does not change the status: it is the booking's `deposit_total` (the report's "avans olindi" is confirmed + a deposit).
BookingStatus.title: BookingStatus

CancelReason.description: Why an order was cancelled or rejected (orders.cancel_reason). Every cancellation made from now on carries one; rows cancelled before the column existed have none. Only `no_show` counts towards the cash pickup ban (Order::cashPickupBanApplies).
CancelReason.title: CancelReason

CashMovementType.description: cash_movements.type: what moved money into or out of the drawer (POS_SPEC 2.3, research R21, L7, L10). The cashier records `cash_in`, `cash_out`, `wage` (to an employee) and `purchase` (bazaar shopping) by hand; the others are written by the shift, sale and refund flows themselves. Booking deposits and nasiya repayments taken in cash (P3-17), and cash deposit refunds, are read from their own tables by the shift report (ShiftReport), not copied here.
CashMovementType.title: CashMovementType

CourierType.description: Whose courier it is: the restaurant's own staff or the platform's fleet. Dispatch by type comes in phase 4.
CourierType.title: CourierType

DiningTableKind.description: What a place on the floor map is (dining_tables.kind, P3-12): a plain table, a room ("xona", "kabinka": a long session with a room fee and often a minimum spend) or a tapchan.
DiningTableKind.title: DiningTableKind

ErrorResponse.description: Xato javobi: `success: false` va foydalanuvchiga ko'rsatiladigan `message`.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FireMode.description: When a POS line goes to the kitchen (order_items.fire_mode, P3-12, docs/POS_SPEC.md §2.6): with the next "send" (`now`), or only when it is sent by name (`hold`: a later course, a pre-order with its due time).
FireMode.title: FireMode

IntegrationConnectionStatus.description: P4-31: a connection's state. `paused` is set by the team (Integratsiyalar, with a reason); `disconnected` by the health check when the outside system stops answering (phase 5).
IntegrationConnectionStatus.title: IntegrationConnectionStatus

IntegrationDirection.description: P4-31: which way a connection carries orders (docs/PHASE5_PLAN.md 3): A — a RIZQIM marketplace order goes to the venue's own POS; B — an aggregator's order (Yandex Eats, Uzum Tezkor) comes to Rizqim POS.
IntegrationDirection.title: IntegrationDirection

IntegrationEventDirection.description: P4-31: whether a journaled call came to RIZQIM (a webhook, an aggregator's request) or went out from it.
IntegrationEventDirection.title: IntegrationEventDirection

IntegrationEventStatus.description: P4-31: a journaled call's state (docs/PHASE5_PLAN.md 4.4): waiting, sent, confirmed by the other side, failed (it will be retried: 1, 2, 4 ... 32 minutes) and dead (out of retries; an alert).
IntegrationEventStatus.title: IntegrationEventStatus

IntegrationMode.description: P4-31: a sandbox connection never touches a real kitchen or real money (docs/PHASE5_PLAN.md 4.6).
IntegrationMode.title: IntegrationMode

IntegrationProvider.description: P4-31: the outside systems an IntegrationConnection can point at (docs/PHASE5_PLAN.md 3, 4.3). Phase 5 adds adapters for them; adding a provider later is adding a case here.
IntegrationProvider.title: IntegrationProvider

InvoiceKind.description: P4-21: what a subscription invoice bills. monthly: a month that ended (base fee, extra devices, discount; for a yearly subscription only its extra devices); yearly: a yearly term in advance; upgrade: the prorated difference of an immediate upgrade of a yearly subscription.
InvoiceKind.title: InvoiceKind

KitchenItemStatus.description: Where an order line is in the kitchen (order_items.kitchen_status, P2-11): `pending` until a cook bumps it on the kitchen display, then `ready`. P3-12 (docs/POS_SPEC.md §2.8, §10.3): a POS line is `pending` while it is only on the order (not sent yet, or held), `sent` once the POS sends it to the kitchen, then `ready`, and `served` when it reached the guests; `void` when it was taken off the order ("O'CHIRILDI"). An online (Telegram, mobile) line keeps the P2-11 meaning: `pending` is in the kitchen from the start (it has no sent_at and no fire_mode).
KitchenItemStatus.title: KitchenItemStatus

MenuUnit.description: How a product variant is sold (product_variants.unit): by the piece (portion, bottle) or by weight/volume, whose price is per kilogram or litre and whose quantity may be a fraction in steps of quantity_step (docs/MENU.md).
MenuUnit.title: MenuUnit

MinSpendMode.description: How a room's minimum spend ("obyazalovka", R4) is set (dining_tables.min_spend_mode, P3-12): once for the room, or per guest (× guests_count).
MinSpendMode.title: MinSpendMode

ModifierGroupRequest.description:
The body of POST /owner/modifier-groups and PUT /owner/modifier-groups/{id} (P1-21; P2-30: a form request, so the
OpenAPI document and the generated clients carry it). The permission (menu.manage) is the route's; the checks that
need the store (linked variants, bounds) stay in ModifierGroupController.
ModifierGroupRequest.title: ModifierGroupRequest

OrderChannel.description: Where an order came from (orders.channel). One Order model serves every channel (docs/ROADMAP.md): the kitchen sees them all, the stop-list reaches them all, and channel prices/visibility (channel_prices) differ per channel.
OrderChannel.title: OrderChannel

Permission.description: What a store staff member may do. Each role gets a default set (App\Services\Auth\RolePermissions) that an owner can adjust per store (role_permission_overrides); App\Services\Auth\PermissionService resolves the effective set, and the Gate answers `$user->can('orders.cancel', $order)` with it (branch scoping included).
Permission.title: Permission

PlatformRole.description: P4-11: the RIZQIM team's roles in the Boshqaruv markazi (platform/admin, docs/PHASE4_PLAN.md §5). A user is platform staff when users.platform_role is set. What each role may do is App\Services\Admin\PlatformRolePermissions (defaults) with the superadmin's overrides (platform_role_permissions); `superadmin` is fixed: everything. Only `superadmin` is also users.role = super_admin (the old store-level super admin); the other roles are users.role = platform, which holds no store-level permission at all.
PlatformRole.title: PlatformRole

PosSyncOperationType.description: What a till may do offline (docs/POS_SPEC.md §5.1), each applied through the POS domain services on sync: open a walk-in or room order, add a round, send lines to the kitchen, void an unsent line, mark a line served, make one bill, take cash or card for it, close the order.
PosSyncOperationType.title: PosSyncOperationType

ProductKind.description: What a menu item is on a receipt (products.kind, P3-11): a dish (taom, ichimlik) or a service the store sells like a dish (cooking from the guest's own food, kazan rent, a set menu service). Both need an MXIK code before a fiscal store may sell them; the kind tells the panel and the receipt which MXIK group (10202001 or 10202002) fits.
ProductKind.title: ProductKind

StoreApplicationStage.description: P4-22: the onboarding pipeline of a store application (docs/PHASE4_PLAN.md §4.3): ariza → tekshiruv → menyu → qurilmalar → o'qitish → sinov → faol, or rad etildi. Every stage has a checklist: an item is done when ticked by hand or, for the ones marked `detect`, when the store shows it (App\Services\Admin\Stores\ApplicationPipeline). Moving forward needs the required items of every stage passed; `menu` and later need the store created (convert).
StoreApplicationStage.title: StoreApplicationStage

StoreFormat.description: P4-22: what kind of food place a store application is (the public form's `format`).
StoreFormat.title: StoreFormat

SubscriptionStatus.description: A store subscription's state (docs/BILLING.md). Only `cancelled` rows are history; every other status is the store's current subscription, whose plan sets its commission and monthly fee. P4-21: `locked` — an invoice is unpaid more than config('billing.dunning.lock_after_days') days after its due date: settings and features outside the plan close (App\Services\Finance\Billing\Entitlements); the till keeps taking payments and printing receipts. Paying unlocks at once.
SubscriptionStatus.title: SubscriptionStatus
